QUESTION OF THE WEEK - The June quarter has just ended, so economists were asked for their preliminary GDP forecasts. A strong result is widely expected with net exports and stocks seen as large contributors and private consumption only a small contributor or possibly a small detraction.
The inclusion of a A$500 million Navy frigate in the May trade data means net exports will be a solid contributor.
However, some economists said the frigate may also be reflected in a rundown in manufacturing stocks, and so stocks may not be as strong a contributor asmmight be first thought.

Stocks fell 2.1 percent or A$1.3 billion in the March quarter. While they may fall again in the June quarter, the fall would need to be larger than the first quarter drop to make a negative contribution to GDP.

The quarterly forecast would translate into an annual growth rate of 3.1 percent, and following on from the 0.9 percent rise in first quarter growth, would add weight to the argument that the economy has passed its softest point, analysts said.

LABOUR FORCE - A large headline figure is expected, with the median forecast seen reversing the 40,300 fall posted in June. But even if employment rises by 40,000 in June, it will have only risen by 24,000, or 6,000 a month, over the first half of 1997. There are some signs labour demand is improving in data series such as the ANZ and ABS job vacancy measures, but business surveys are still showing a subdued outlook for employment. Unemployment is expected to come in above 8.7 percent, making it the 11th time in the 1996/97 fiscal year that it was at 8.6 percent or higher. A weak figure, and that could
include a rise up to 30,000, would be bullish for those looking for a rate cut, while it would take a rise of close to 100,000 to put a serious dent in the rate cut case, economists said.

HOUSING FINANCE - After the huge jump in April, a large corrective fall is forecast, with most of it expected to show up in refinancing. The key figure to establish what is happening in terms of the housing recovery will be in new lending, and that is expected to show a rise.
